albums.blurb: Mahavishnu Orchestra was guitarist John McLaughlin's pioneering fusion band, formed after his stints with Miles Davis on In a Silent Way and Bitches Brew. Birds of Fire is the second album by the original lineup — McLaughlin, drummer Billy Cobham, keyboardist Jan Hammer, violinist Jerry Goodman, and bassist Rick Laird — and the last studio record that quintet completed before splintering. It is entirely instrumental: ten tracks of interlocking odd meters, twin guitar-violin melodies, and Cobham's polyrhythmic drumming, compressed into under forty minutes.
albums.reception: It became the group's commercial peak, reaching No. 15 on the Billboard 200 and earning RIAA gold certification — a rare feat for an all-instrumental jazz-rock record.

albums.blurb: Jacob Collier broke out as a teenager posting split-screen videos from his family's music room in North London, harmonizing every part himself, which led Quincy Jones to take him on. In My Room, released in July 2016, is his debut album, written, performed, and produced almost entirely alone in that same room. It mixes originals like "Hideaway" with radically rebuilt covers, including the Beach Boys' "In My Room," Stevie Wonder's "You and I," and the Flintstones theme.
albums.reception: Two arrangements from the album — "You and I" and "Flintstones" — each won a Grammy Award at the 2017 ceremony, in the instrumental/a cappella and instruments-and-vocals arranging categories respectively.

albums.blurb: The Sundays formed in London around singer Harriet Wheeler and guitarist David Gavurin, and their January 1990 debut on Rough Trade distilled the jangling guitar lineage of the Smiths into something airier, carried by Wheeler's high, glassy voice. Reading, Writing and Arithmetic is the first of only three albums the famously press-shy band released before quietly withdrawing from music in the late 1990s, which has given the record an enduring cult standing among 1990s British guitar-pop debuts.
albums.reception: The album reached No. 4 on the UK Albums Chart and No. 39 on the Billboard 200, while its single "Here's Where the Story Ends" topped Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart in the US.
